source.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
source.authors: Akhilesh Deepak Gotmare; N. Keskar; Caiming Xiong; R. Socher

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied, including appendices; no truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training outcomes and analyzes learning-rate schedules on CIFAR-10, testing the warmup-related portion of V6 with its own controlled runs. It does not test the broader initialization, width, depth-with-shortcuts, or zero-error claims.
record.gate_note: Reports training accuracy for mode-connectivity curves in Appendix Figures 8–9, but the supplied text gives no numerical values or explicit description of those training-accuracy outcomes. The warmup experiments report validation accuracy and layer similarity, not training classification error or whether batch normalization speeds training. Other discussion of SGDR and distillation does not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests warmup, cosine restarts, mode connectivity and distillation, but none of V1–V6 as stated. Warmup comparisons retain batch normalization and do not test its benefit; large learning rates are not measured against a stability threshold. Training-accuracy figures lack readable values or explicit near-zero-error findings in the supplied text.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors interpret warmup as preventing unstable changes in deeper layers, with temporary freezing producing similar outcomes in their tested cases; question explanations of cosine restarts based on escaping local minima; and hypothesize that transferred distillation knowledge is concentrated in deeper layers.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies learning-rate schedules, mode connectivity and representational similarity; it does not use the claimed training-error measurement or test the listed original recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Warmup effects are studied across batch size and learning-rate configurations, VGG-11 versus ResNet-18/32, and warmup versus freezing the fully connected stack. The authors state that whether results generalize to ImageNet remains to be shown.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, warmup preserves greater initial-to-post-warmup representational similarity in VGG-11's fully connected layers than large-batch training without warmup. Initially freezing those layers produces comparable validation performance; analogous experiments use ResNet-18 and ResNet-32.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Warmup can stabilize early changes in deeper layers during large-batch training, and temporarily freezing those layers can produce similar outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected VGG-16 SGDR checkpoint pairs have training-loss barriers along straight interpolations, whereas the selected SGD pairs do not. Projected loss surfaces do not identify the SGDR checkpoints as separate local minima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cosine restarts can produce trajectories crossing interpolation barriers without establishing escape from isolated local minima.

fits_no_version.finding: Low-loss connecting curves are found between VGG-16 models trained with different optimizers, initialization variance, batch sizes, schedules, regularization and augmentation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mode connectivity persists across several changes in training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Distilled students attain best validation accuracy of 85.18%, versus 83.01% for hard-label training across five runs per setup; teacher–student representational differences are concentrated in deeper layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distillation's representational effects are concentrated primarily in deeper layers in the tested convolutional networks.

record.problems: For the warmup claim, the supplied results report validation accuracy and CCA similarity rather than training accuracy or training error; key accuracy outcomes are in figures without numerical values. ResNet results are figure-only, and the authors state that generality to larger datasets such as ImageNet remains unshown.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained. Appendix Figures 8–9 show training accuracy for mode-connectivity curves, but the supplied text does not give values or describe the outcomes explicitly. Figure 4 and Figure 15 report validation-accuracy curves for warmup comparisons, which do not measure the training-speed claim in V6.

untested.parts: Whether gradient training reaches near-zero training classification error, including label corruption and dependence on model size, stopping or regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction with extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization alternatives.
Initialization effects on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth. The altered-initialization mode-connectivity experiment does not measure these effects.
Recovery above an initial stability threshold, accompanying curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence conditions.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and normalization-free training using Fixup. Warmup is not a component of this version.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification and V6 tested_not_extracted designation. There are no extracted rows to fix. Unreadable training-accuracy figures are already declared in rows_left_out and do not establish a V1 verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping and regularization effects.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and effects of extra student neurons.
Plain versus residual depth effects, special plain-network initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep convolutional training.
Training above stability limits, curvature or sharpness behavior, low training loss, and divergence.

The paper tests warmup and freezing the fully connected stack in VGG-11, ResNet-18 and ResNet-32 under large-batch training, but reports validation accuracy and representational similarity rather than training speed or a batch-normalization comparison. The CIFAR-10 validation accuracy outcomes appear in figures without numerical values.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
